- Structure: 1 — you stated actions but not S-T-A-R order.

- Specificity: 1 — method named but no tools, timeframe, constraints, or your role.

Result: I delivered the forecast two days early and the board used it to set pricing and inventory actions that avoided an expected shortfall."

- [three days] — how fast you actually had to deliver

- [three public comps] — or how you benchmarked

- Structure: 3/4 — you used [your skill] order clearly (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

One concrete improvement: add a single numeric outcome (a percent, dollar amount, or days saved) or a precise constraint you overcame (e.g., "delivered in 2 of 3 business days" or "reduced forecast error from 12% to 4%"). That one number raises credibility immediately.

You don't have any Lincoln International items on file yet (no postings, no drafts, no invite). I'll prepare a focused final-round plan and mock questions now assuming this is a standard analyst final round for M&A: technical case/modeling, fit/behavior, and a short partner conversation. I assume a 45–75 minute interview with a mix of technical and fit; tell me if the format or time is different.
Preparation plan (do these in order)
1) One-page prep sheet to memorize (6 lines) — I’ll give it below.
2) Quick technical refresh (20–30 minutes) — DCF steps, comps logic, LBO drivers, basic 3-statement walkthrough and key formulas.
3) Two focused mock questions now (I’ll ask them below): you answer, I’ll score and rewrite your best 60–90s answers.
4) Closing and logistics — five smart questions to ask partners and a short day-of checklist.
One-page prep sheet to memorize (one line each)
- 30‑second story: current role, what you do, why Lincoln (M&A/advisory focus + specific reason) and your goal [fill specifics].
- Technical anchor 1 — DCF: three steps to value, terminal value choices, where sensitivity matters.
- Technical anchor 2 — Comps/Precedent: what multiples measure, when to use EV/Revenue vs EV/EBITDA, key comparability issues.
- Technical anchor 3 — LBO basics: IRR levers — purchase price, margin improvement, leverage, exit multiple.
- Two deal bullets (1–2 lines each): your role, the challenge, what you did, and the concrete result or learning.
- Closing line + question: one-liner tying you to Lincoln and two concise questions to ask partners.
Key technical facts to have crisp (say out loud)
- DCF skeleton: forecast unlevered free cash flows → discount at WACC → add PV of terminal value → enterprise value → subtract net debt → equity value → per-share if needed.
- Unlevered FCF formula to recall: NOPAT + D&A - CapEx - ΔNWC (or EBIT*(1-tax) + D&A - CapEx - ΔNWC).
- Terminal value: Gordon growth vs exit multiple; know when each is appropriate and how to set a reasonable growth or exit multiple.
- WACC intuition: market-value weights, after-tax cost of debt, equity cost rises with risk; higher leverage lowers WACC to a point but raises risk.
- Multiples takeaways: EV/Revenue for early/high-growth or low-margin companies; EV/EBITDA when margins are meaningful and comparable.
- LBO IRR drivers: entry multiple, exit multiple, leverage, operating improvements (margin expansion) and cashflow-driven debt paydown.

Three short behavioral story frames (STAR, 60–90s each)
- Team conflict/disagreement: situation, what you did (listen + data), concrete action and result.
- High-pressure deliverable: how you prioritized, tradeoffs, outcome and what you learned.
- Mistake then recovery: what went wrong, immediate fix, what you changed so it didn’t recur.
Two deal bullets to prepare (write these now in your words)
- Deal A: your role, specific task, what you solved, quant result or lesson.
- Deal B: same format — pick one where you had modeling, diligence or client-facing ownership.

Two mock questions — answer one paragraph each now; I’ll score and rewrite into tight 60–90s answers
1) Behavioral: "Walk me through a deal you worked on from start to finish. What was your role and one concrete challenge you solved?"
2) Technical: "Walk me through a 3-year DCF at a high level and name the main sensitivities I'd stress in a sensitivity table."
Five sharp questions to ask at the end (pick 1–2)
- "What makes someone successful in Lincoln’s analyst program in the first 12 months?"
- "Can you tell me about a recent deal where the team faced an unexpected obstacle and how it was resolved?"
- "How do teams balance client work with training and mentorship for junior analysts?"
- "What are typical next steps for analysts who want to specialize in [sector you care about]?"
- "What do you most enjoy about working at Lincoln?"
Day‑of checklist (quick)
- Copies of resume (2), laptop charged, Excel and calculator open, interviewers’ names/roles, quiet space, notepad and pen, 10–15 minute buffer, water. Have a printed one-line of your 30s story and two deal bullets on paper.

What I’ll score when you answer the mock questions
- Structure (clear beginning, middle, end)
- Evidence (concrete actions you took)
- Specificity (numbers, timeline, tools)
I’ll rewrite each into a 60–90s answer you can memorize.

Next step
Answer the two mock questions above now (one paragraph each). I’ll score and edit them into final, memorized responses and give the short technical refresh and sample partner-closing lines.
Saved nothing yet about your Lincoln interview. Is the assumed format (45–75 min with technical, modeling and partner fit) right?

You don't have any applications or a resume on file yet. The one step that starts this is: paste the resume you want used, or name which saved posting is “the first one.”

Here’s exactly what I will prepare and place on the application card for the first posting you pick, field by field, with where each piece of content comes from and what you must confirm before anything is sent. I assume a standard online job form plus an optional cover-letter upload; if the employer uses a custom form I’ll adapt these fields to match it.
1) Job reference
- What goes in: employer name, job title, job location, the posting link, and the employer’s internal posting ID (when provided).
- Source: the posting you choose.
- Your action: confirm that the card shows the correct posting before sending.

2) Resume PDF (required)
- What goes in: a one-page or two-page PDF resume tailored to the posting.
- Source: the resume you paste here or your confirmed profile facts. I will not invent or confirm facts for you.
- Defaults I’ll use if you don’t tell me: availability = “Available immediately”; I will leave work authorization blank for you to fill.
- Your action: review and approve the PDF in the extension before any submission.
3) Cover letter / short note (optional)
- What goes in: a concise cover letter (~150–300 words) that highlights the posting’s top requirements and 1–2 achievements.
- Source: your pasted resume / confirmed facts; any missing specifics (numbers, employer names, months) will be left in [brackets] for you to fill.
- Your action: edit/approve before it’s attached or sent.
4) Contact details (top-of-resume fields and form fields)
- What goes in: full name, personal email, phone number, city/state (or “Remote”), LinkedIn URL if you want it included.
- Source: exactly what you type here when I ask for it (I won’t use account email or guess).
- Your action: confirm these exactly as you want them printed.

5) Work authorization / visa status
- What goes in: the exact phrase you provide (e.g., “US citizen,” “Authorized to work in US without sponsorship,” “Need H‑1B”).
- Source: you must type it; I will not infer.
- Your action: provide or confirm on the card.
6) Salary expectations / current compensation (when asked)
- What goes in: numbers or a range only if you give them; otherwise left blank.
- Source: what you tell me in chat.
- Your action: supply or leave blank; approve the draft.

7) Availability / earliest start date
- What goes in: the date or notice period you provide, or “Available immediately” as a default.
- Source: you or the default.
- Your action: confirm or correct on the card.
8) Screening / pre‑screen questions (yes/no, multiple choice, short text answers included in the employer form)
- What goes in: answers drafted from your confirmed facts or from the resume you paste. If a screening question asks for years of experience, I’ll draft the numeric answer from your resume; if missing, I’ll leave a placeholder like [X years] for you to fill.
- Source: your resume/confirmed facts and the posting text.
- Your action: review and edit every answer on the card.
9) Work-history fields (if the employer requests discrete entries)
- What goes in: role title, employer name, dates (month/year), location, and 2–4 tailored achievement bullets for each role.
- Source: the resume you paste or confirmed facts. Missing months/dates stay in [brackets].
- Your action: verify accuracy of dates and bullets.

10) Education fields (degree, school, dates)
- What goes in: exactly what you provided in the resume or confirmed facts.
- Source: your resume/confirmed facts.
- Your action: review for correctness.
11) Skills and certifications checkboxes or text fields
- What goes in: keywords from the posting matched to skills you confirmed; unconfirmed skills will be left for you to check.
- Source: posting keywords + your confirmed facts or pasted resume.
- Your action: confirm which skills to include.

12) Attachments (portfolio, transcripts, certificates, references)
- What goes in: files or links you provide. I will note them on the card and attach only the files you gave.
- Source: files you upload or links you provide in chat.
- Your action: confirm attachments to upload.
13) Additional employer-specific fields (current employer, manager name, LinkedIn profile)
- What goes in: only what you provide or what’s on your resume; I will not guess.
- Source: you.
- Your action: fill/approve any optional fields.

14) Optional referral or employee name (if you provide one)
- What goes in: the name and email exactly as you type them.
- Source: you.
- Your action: confirm permission to include the referral.

15) EEO / Diversity / Self-ID fields
- What goes in: only what you type; otherwise left blank.
- Source: you.
- Your action: fill if you wish.
16) Final submission options and privacy choices
- What goes in: sensible defaults (resume PDF preferred; do not opt in to extra sharing unless you say so), or the choices the employer requires.
- Source: posting cues and your instruction.
- Your action: confirm final choices on the card.

17) Notes to recruiter / optional message field
- What goes in: a single short sentence tailored to the job—e.g., “I’m excited to apply for [role]; my background in [skill] matches [requirement].” I’ll draft it with any missing specifics in [brackets].
- Your action: approve or edit.
What I will not do automatically
- I will not submit the application without your explicit approval in the Trainee extension/card. The extension shows every field above and sends only when you confirm.
- I will not invent contact details, authorization, dates, pay numbers or achievements.
- I will not confirm any drafted facts for you; anything new I save from your pasted resume will be draft facts that you must confirm before they’re used in a tailored resume.

One sensible default I will use if you don’t tell me: availability = “Available immediately.” For everything else I’ll either leave it blank or place a [bracketed prompt] on the card for you to fill.
Next step: paste the resume you want used here, or tell me which posting is the “first one” (the job title and company). Which do you want?
